ONE HOME: a derived `realtime: boolean` on the verdict, **a LITERAL type on the other three variants ∴ a `running-behind` claiming realtime WOULD NOT COMPILE** (§V960). **TOLERANCE COUNTED ∈ FRAMES OF THE WINDOW, NEVER ∈ PERCENT: `slack = min(2, max(0.5, expectedFrames / 10))`, `realtime = recentFrameCount >= expectedFrames − slack`** — CEILING 2 frames (one is pure counting resolution: a loop dead on 60 fps reads 89 ∨ 90 depending where `now` fell; the second is one genuinely dropped frame per 1.5 s; a third is a shortfall a person can SEE); A TENTH OF THE WINDOW BETWEEN (2 frames is noise @ 60 fps & a SIXTH of the rate @ 6 fps — uncapped, a 6 fps project would read realtime @ 4.67); FLOOR 0.5 (NOT a tolerance but a ROUNDING RULE: `recent` is an integer & `expectedFrames` fractional — 3 fps = 4.5 — so the threshold rounds to nearest instead of demanding a count NO PHASE CAN REACH). **a flat percentage gets it BACKWARDS — 5 % is four frames of slack @ 60 fps & less than one @ 24, LOOSEST WHERE QUANTIZATION MATTERS LEAST — which is why there is no 0.95.** FOUR STATES: live+realtime → green dot **Realtime**; live-under-rate → error dot **Behind**; running-behind → error **Behind**; browser-throttled → warn **Throttled**; paused → dim **Paused**. **the DOT answers ONE question (realtime or not — green is yes) & the HUE says WHOSE FAULT. WHAT THE REFERENCE SHOWS (read frame by frame, 10 s, a node graph): (1) a wire dragged from an output is white with a round tip at the cursor; (2) IN RANGE of an input it can take, the port gains a ring in the connection's colour and a jagged ELECTRIC ARC plays between the wire's tip and the port (a main bolt and a thinner branch, re-drawn every few frames), while the tip stays with the cursor — the arc is the sign that letting go here will connect; (3) ON RELEASE the wire snaps to the port and takes the colour along its whole length, the port's dot fills, two rings pulse outward from the port and fade, a bright bar lights on the node's edge at the port and TRAVELS along the border both ways — up round the top-left corner and along the top, down round the bottom-left and along the bottom — with a soft glow bleeding into the node behind it, gone in well under a second; (4) the row gains a tick and the node's status line changes when its last input arrives; (5) grabbing a connected end pulls the wire off again (white, the tick goes), and the arc returns as it nears a port. wanted in Loom's canvas, built from the reference and not by dressing what exists: the range a release connects from is the range the arc shows (one number, also the edge-reconnect range); only a port the wire may connect to attracts, and a refused port says why in its own way; the colour is the port type's token; nothing in the effect moves a node's box (§V389), costs React work per frame, or is left in the DOM after it ends; reduced motion keeps the ring and the colour and drops the arc and the travel. design note first (what xyflow gives, where the effect layer lives, zoom behaviour), then build, with a recording from the running app for the owner. **LANDED `25884800` (design note, `docs/wire-snap-design-2026-10-06.md`) + `085b2b37` (verified on main: typecheck; the gates 3,594). A RECORDING FROM THE RUNNING APP WENT TO THE OWNER (100 % and 35 %).** THE REFERENCE MEASURED AT FULL RATE beside the build: range 90–100 px (14 dot radii) → `WIRE_RANGE_PX = 48` (14 of Loom's 3.5 px radii); ring in 66 ms → 70 ms; the arc a corner every 7 px, redrawn at 15 Hz, one thin branch → a corner every 6 px, 15 Hz, the same branch; two rings in 470 ms → 460 and 360 ms; the bar both ways, half the border each, near linear → the same; the whole snap 0.75 s → 0.72 s (0.3 s still under reduced motion). THE RANGE IS ONE NUMBER (`src/editor/edges/wire-range.ts`): 48 px ON SCREEN at every zoom below 100 % and 48 graph px above it, written to the library's `connectionRadius` when the zoom changes (the library's default of 20 was 7 px on screen at 35 %); the arc is drawn from the library's own `toHandle` and `isValid`, so the arc and the release cannot disagree. A REFUSING PORT shows a dashed ring in the dim text colour and, after a quarter second, a caption in the Connections panel's words (`takes texture2d<float,4,linear>`); it never sparks. the effect lives in the library's own connection-line layer, renders once, and is driven by a store subscription writing attributes and one rAF loop that runs only while a port sparks; the snap plays only when the bus reports `applied`, leaves nothing in the DOM, and sits outside the node's own element (§V389: boxes identical before, during and after). BEHAVIOUR THAT CHANGED: a press on a CONNECTED input's dot now pulls that wire off (it used to start a second wire out of the input); a pulled wire let go in the open is DISCONNECTED (one undo entry), on a port that takes it is one "Move connection" patch, back on its own port is no command; only the input end can be pulled; the wire in flight is white and the library's green and red handle rings are gone. T1604b|x|**ONE RENDER PASS PER TARGET, NOT PER DRAW (P2 of the same profile).** every draw of every geometry is its own render pass: 200 render passes a frame over about 20 targets for sentinel-bot's hinged document, and each pass pays encode, submit and (for an indirect draw) ~0.05 ms of GPU. wanted: the Render's draws into one target (the lit colour, each G-buffer layer, each shadow face) share a pass in plan order; this also amortises the indirect-draw cost that §T1581b's F1 introduced. design first: what the plan IR's pass means when it holds several draws, the timer spans, the loop-region rule. **DESIGN WRITTEN (`docs/geometry-cost-profile-2026-10-05.md`, "P2, design") AND RULED:** encoder only — the plan stays one pass per draw; the backend groups a run of consecutive draws into one device render pass (same target, only the first may clear, nothing but draws between; a run never crosses a loop marker); one pure function over the pass list shared by the encoder, the inspector and previews. counted on the hinged plan: 200 device passes → 43 with that rule, ~19 if the Render also emits each G-buffer layer's draws together (the reorder is part of the row). `updateUniforms({ passId })`, the orbit's `passIds` and the pipeline inspector's reading are untouched. TIMER SPANS: a run has one span, billed to the run with its members shown as share-holders (no invented division), and one pass per draw is encoded again while the performance panel or timeline is open. **LANDED `99b5ec84` + `e93add0c` (main's tree is byte for byte the worker's tested tip; confirmed on main: typecheck, `render-pass-runs.test.ts`, `skipped-draw`, `hub`, `performance-panel`, `composition-wiring` 140, and on Dawn `render-pass-runs.gpu.test.ts` + `timing-drops.gpu.test.ts` 12; the worker ran 37 named files 636, 22 Dawn files, the gates 3540, the build).** A RUN (`renderPassRuns`, `plan.ts`, the one definition): consecutive draws of ONE NODE into one target, of which only the first may clear; an effect, a dispatch, a swap, a loop marker, another target, another node or a clearing draw ends it. the Render now emits each G-buffer layer's draws together after everything that draws the colour (additive last, extending the lit run). TWO DEPARTURES FROM THE DESIGN, RULED BY THE LEAD AS BUILT: (1) one node per run, so a node's GPU figure stays a measurement (shortens no run in the eleven plans checked); (2) A MULTISAMPLED TARGET IS LEFT A PASS PER DRAW — grouped, the consumer's colour (rgba16float, 4× MSAA) differed from one pass per draw on 0 to 8 of 230,400 pixels a frame by one unit in the last place where the claws meet the last rings; cause not found, no fixture reproduces it, every single-sampled target is byte-identical, and the frame must not depend on whether the performance panel is open (§T1614b). TIMING: a run has one GPU span named head plus count (`head+13`); the panel holds a demand WHILE ON SCREEN (a hidden dock pane stays mounted, §V96) and the backend then encodes one pass per draw (`LoomBackend.setExactPassTiming`, `TelemetrySource.demandPassDetail`, `TelemetryHub.attachPassDetailSwitch`, `PassTimingRow.run`, harness option `exactPassTiming`). WHERE THE LIVE FRAME GOES NOW: five cube shadows 7.0 ms of 13.9 (50%), the finish chain with its Depth and Normal layers 3.9 ms (28%); by GPU time the cheapest shadows to lose are `light_body` and `light_lamp2` (1.2 ms each), the others 1.6 ms each. DESIGN IN PROGRESS. **DESIGN LANDED `559efc51` (`docs/rope-solver-design-2026-10-05.md`), RULED BY THE LEAD as recommended, pending the consumer's review.** D1 THE METHOD IS NOT THE ROW'S SKETCH: red/black relaxation on kernel steps leaves the worst segment 51% long at 16 dispatches a frame on the consumer's motion (31% with long-range attachments — which are also patented, US 9,070,220 B2 — and follow-the-leader keeps length but gains energy, tip 88 m/s against 41). chosen: XPBD in small steps with each strand's stretch constraints solved TOGETHER — the system XPBD relaxes one constraint at a time is tridiagonal on a chain, and one GPU thread per strand solves it exactly in a walk like Curve Frames' (Han & Harada 2013, Goldenthal 2007): worst segment 0.012% at 16, 8 and 4 dispatches; exact when hanging; momentum-conserving. its one limit: a step shorter than a transverse wave's crossing of one segment (54 links: 2 substeps at 1 g, 12 at 55 g), with Notch's Max Stretch as a positions-only guard past it. figures from a float64 CPU model written for the design (`scratchpad/rope-model/`), nothing measured on a device yet. NODE `pointRope` ("Rope", kind `rope`): strips in, the same strips out, `position` replaced, `velocity` published; Notch's vocabulary (Update Rate 240, Min/Max Update Steps 1/16, Iterations 4, Gravity, Damping, Force, Mass, Rest Length Scale, Stretch as a compliance, Max Stretch 2%, Bend, Collision Thickness, Friction); anchors First / Second / Last as weights 0–1 with Map mode plus a per-point pin attribute, each pinning to the INCOMING point interpolated across the frame's steps (a 3 s quintic grab moves a claw 46.8 mm a frame; a stepped weight would move it 4,172 mm — the pop); two anchors out of reach: the earlier holds; Teleport Distance with Carry or Reset; time by Notch's rule `steps = clamp(round(delta × rate), min, max)`, no accumulator; collision with a floor, a second pointset (spheres, capsule chains, Inside for a tube), a height field, a WGSL distance function. its own shader module, one dispatch per update step on the kernel-steps region. D3 needs two small changes in `compiler/substeps.ts` (a rate form on the steps declaration; one unstepped dispatch beside the stepped one). slices: 1 strand and time, 2 anchors, 3 colliders, 4 bend, 5 distance function, 6 height field; follow-ups R1–R17 (long strands, cloth, self and strand-strand collision, twist, pre-roll). FOUND: sentinel-bot's world jumps 960 m once a lap (`speed_travel` loops), which any stateful rope will see — Teleport Carry is exact for it. **CONSUMER'S REVIEW (shaderloom-f1, 2026-10-06): NO OBJECTION to the method or the rulings; one requirement and an order.** (R1, REQUIRED) A BEND LIMIT: its rings are rigid pieces at a 0.06 m pitch (shell radius 0.049 m on a 0.036 m spine) and intersect once a joint turns past about 0.4 rad; its rig test holds every bend to a radius of 0.15 m or more. Bend Stiffness 0 lets a slack chain fold flat (a slack loop's bottom, the socket when the claw is close, a tail piled on the deck), and a spring toward straight gives no bound. wanted: a LIMIT, "no joint turns more than this angle" (a minimum bend radius), as a guard after the solve like Max Stretch, with Bend Stiffness as the soft part under it; test: 54 links, both ends pinned 0.5 m apart, 3.2 m of rope, the largest turn at any joint. goes with slice 4. (R2) SLICE ORDER for this consumer: 1, 2, 4 (with the limit), 5, then 3 (the body capsule); 6 never. (R3) slice 2 must measure a FAST MOVING PIN at weight 1: the claw's target crosses rung to rung at about 4 m/s every stride and about 8 m/s in the attack. T1623b|.|**NAMED POINT AND SPOT LIGHTS IN THE GRID (accepted limitation 2 of §T1589b's design, `docs/lights-from-pointset-design-2026-10-06.md` section 9).** A Light in Single mode is an unrolled block evaluated by every lit pixel. with a Range it could be a record and be culled (probe: 0.72 against 0.26 ms at sixteen lights of which two reach a pixel), and a casting one would take its shadow inside the loop by a switch over the slots. it changes the text of a Render that has both, and for unlimited lights the blocks are faster (1.38 against 1.84 ms at 64). decide on a document with many named Lights. **NOW REQUIRED, NOT A WEIGHING (§B260, 2026-10-06):** the design's reason to leave named Lights as unrolled blocks ("1.38 against 1.84 ms at 64") was taken on a raw probe without a clock reference; in the engine the unrolled blocks are 18.7 ms at 64 lights and a loop 1.11 ms, with cold pipeline creation 572 against 119 ms. ruling L5 of §T1589b is reversed: named NON-CASTING Lights (point, spot, and directional as always-walked rows) become records walked by the loop; casting Lights stay blocks, each under its own guard. built as the slice straight after §T1589b slice 1; it removes §B260's stopgap and moves every multi-light Render's text once (fingerprints re-stamped, exact pixel claims re-derived, in that one landing). the gate it makes possible: the lit text's size does not grow with the non-casting light count. from the audit (§T1635b): the same landing takes R2 (the instances generator's copy of the light block), R3 (projectors: rows with their cookie and occlusion from an indexable resource, or a bounded exception under §V1029 (d)) and R4 (a casting light's lookup); the shadow matte stops declaring every shadow map. **THE DESIGN IS LANDED AND RULED: ONE LIGHT PATH (`docs/light-cost-investigation-2026-10-06.md` section 11, `24d1fda5`; this row is now its umbrella).** THE PROPERTY: the lit shader's text is the same for any number of lights of any kind; adding a Light, removing one, switching one on or off, turning Cast Shadows on, changing its Type or re-ordering the list creates no shader module and no pipeline — it is a write to a buffer and, for a casting light, one more layer of a texture that exists. EVERY LIGHT IS A ROW of the Render's light table (§T1589b's records, grid and loop): a point of a pointset, a named Light as a set of one, a Projector; the 64-byte record's three free floats carry kind, shadow slot and source number; directional lights and lights with no Range are the first rows, walked by a plain loop whose count is a value; ranged rows go through the grid; loop counts come from the table, never the text (a count in the text is a text per count and invites unrolling). A NEW BACKEND SEAM: values for a REGION OF A BUFFER, carried by the plan and written like a uniform block's, so a named Light's row needs no shader of its own (also the cure of §T1640b). CASTING: two layered targets a Render (`texture_2d_array` of `r32float`, read with `textureLoad` and a layer), one for directional maps and one whose layers are today's 3 × 2 cube atlases; no cube array, no depth texture, no comparison sampler — the lookup stays the texel load and written-out compare the PCF gate pins; the backend's `ring` already is a layered texture with a view a layer; the row carries its slot and the slot's row holds the matrices, softness class and bias; sweeps, caster lists, reach culling and runs carry over; the cap of sixteen sampled textures on casting lights goes. MEASURED PROTOTYPE (the engine's own lit text against the array form derived from it, pictures equal to a half float's step, 2560 × 1440, a reference beside every frame, synthetic maps; blocks as on main / one loop with one array): 1 casting 0.197 / 0.197–0.262 ms; 2: 0.33–0.39 / 0.45–0.46; 4: 0.70–0.72 / 0.79–0.85; 8: 1.51–1.57 / 1.57–1.64; 32 lights of which 8 cast: 15.5–15.9 as main has them, 3.34 guarded, 3.0–3.2 as rows; lit text 7,671 characters at EVERY count against 36,618 at eight casting. softness as loop bounds read from the row costs 1.7×, as a choice between constant loops nothing — so softness is a class the row picks. not measured: directional casting lights in the loop, softness above 1, the sweeps into layers, MSAA, anything through the backend, the projector's cookie copy. RULED BY THE LEAD: D1 a Render with no casting light still carries the lookup and binds the two arrays (else the first Cast Shadows recompiles everything); D2 all five softness kernels always in the text, Shadow Softness becomes a value of the slot's row; D3 the same for projectors, with a cookie ARRAY of one size filled by a copy when a cookie changes (to be measured in its slice; a bounded per-projector binding was the rejected alternative); D4 the buffer-values seam, not a copy dispatch; L4 OF §T1589b IS REVERSED — `kind` STAYS A VALUE so changing a Light's Type recompiles nothing, and a pointset of directional lights is LEGAL (N suns from N points), with a named WARNING when the rows that reach every pixel pass a count (the lead's addition: such rows cost every pixel, and the author must be told). SLICES, each landing green: 1 §T1589b slice 1 (pointset lights, the grid, the loop; in build); 2 the buffer-values seam in the backend, used by nothing yet; 3 named Lights that do not cast are rows (the first slice that moves every shipped Render's lit text: pictures compared across all 63 Renders, exact claims re-run, the text gate arrives); 4 layered shadow targets, the remaining casting blocks reading a literal layer (byte identity on every casting example); 5 casting Lights are rows — the last block goes and with it §B260's stopgap, its gate and its digests; the device-call gate arrives (on the mock host, no module and no pipeline created by any light edit); 6 projectors are rows; 7 the instances generator (primitive instances, points, beams), one exported loop in both. cone and aim (§T1589b's slice 2) come straight after slice 1 for pointset rows, since a row already carries aim and cone, and reach named Lights in slice 3; Lit Only / Lit Exclude get ONE mechanism (the record's source number against a mask on the draw), so editing a list stops being a recompile. 63 shipped Renders: 44 list a light, 27 a casting one (six at most), 12 a projector; `FRAME_ZERO_DIGESTS` does not move. **SLICE 2 LANDED `df542024`: VALUES FOR A REGION OF A BUFFER (verified on main: typecheck; the three `buffer-write` test files with `generated-text`, `kernel-steps`, `animate-parameters`, `render-pass-runs`, `vgpu-backend` 157; on Dawn both `buffer-write` files, `render-pass-runs`, `point-rope`, `scene-render` 46; the gates 58 files / 3,576; the worker ran 26 named files 520 and the build).** a pass kind `write` (`BufferWritePassDescriptor`, `plan.ts`; `src/runtime/backend/buffer-write.ts`): structure is a plain storage buffer, a byte offset, a row as typed 32-bit words (f32, u32, i32), a capacity and where the live count goes; VALUES are the rows and how many are live. it is a pass so that it has an id, and its values then take every road a uniform block's take with no second mechanism: `planUniformValues`, `updateUniforms({ passId })`, the uniform animator, a values-only compile with its rollback, a device rebuild. the backend writes the region's bytes once ahead of the next frame's first pass, only when they moved, and again after a boundary clear or a lost device; T1581b|.|**INSTANCE AN ARBITRARY MESH AT POINTS (engine wish from §T1561b's capability survey, shaderloom-f1 2026-10-05; extends §T1361b).** today geometry mode "instances" / `renderInstances` draws quad, box or octahedron only (`render-instances.ts`, `scene.ts`), with one scalar scale, an orient quaternion and a tint; Material·WGSL is refused on instances (§T1361b) and instances write no normal/albedo/shadow output. wanted: a mesh wired as the instance shape, a per-instance transform (position, orientation, non-uniform scale), Material·WGSL and the G-buffer outputs. the workaround in use: duplicated parts in one GLB, each with a part index, placed per frame by a point kernel (the furnace rig-kernel idiom; sentinel-bot carries 540 ring copies that way). **WANTED BY THE OWNER (relayed by shaderloom-f1, 2026-10-05): "we should support mesh instancing though". IN BUILD. THE CONSUMER'S SHAPE (sentinel-bot):** (1) the instance SHAPE is a mesh pointset (a Mesh File In selection with its triangle topology), drawn once per point of the points input; quad, box and octahedron stay. (2) per instance: position (vec3f), orient (unit quaternion, as today's Map slot), scale as a scalar AND per-axis vec3f, tint (vec4f), one free vec4f passed to the material untouched. (3) Material·WGSL allowed on these draws, the mesh's own vertex attributes intact (normal turned by orient; uv, color, surface, emissive as the file has them), and SurfaceIn carries the instance's free vec4f and the vertex's OBJECT-LOCAL position, so procedural detail sticks to the part. (4) the same citizenship as surface geometry: depth, normal, albedo and shadow outputs; casts and receives shadows from directional and point lights. (5) counted pointsets draw only live instances; the Group predicate culls per instance. (6) size: 2,000–4,000 instances of one ~700-triangle mesh per draw, plus single large parts; one shape per geometry node is enough. **RESEARCH IN (`docs/td-notch-mechanisms-2026-10-05.md`, `fa759eab`):** TD maps each instance attribute from its own source and channel, writes the transform order as a formula, has pivot, rotate-to-vector plus up, an active channel, colour mode, texture index and four custom attributes read in a GLSL MAT; it has no quaternion or matrix instance input until 2026.20000 (keep Loom's quaternion, add rotate-to-vector as the convenience). Notch keeps per-clone state as flat GPU buffers and effectors are an ordered stack of per-clone kernels — Loom's pointset plus kernel chain is that model. take: a SHAPE INDEX per instance (variant pick and kill through one channel); lights as instance data (§T1589b); one sentence on Copy POP ("real copies when you must deform after") vs instancing. the object transform (§T1588b) is designed in the same doc. **BUILD ORDER RULED 2026-10-05 (owner: "order seems good"): §T1588b + §T1581b first, then §T1586b, then §T1587b and §T1589b, then §T1590b and §T1591b; each design-first with the TD/Notch comparison.** **DESIGN LANDED `3106f8f4` (`docs/mesh-instancing-design-2026-10-05.md`, with §T1588b; D1–D17, slices A–G, follow-ups F1–F17). RULED BY THE LEAD 2026-10-05, pending the consumer's review:** O1 Geometry · Instances · Shape: Mesh with a `mesh` input (no new Instancer node); O2 `Frame` on Mesh File In (World | Object | Part, default World, decided at decode); ### Original parallel plan

## §P PARALLEL PLAN

wave = barrier. tracks ∈ wave run concurrent. track owns disjoint paths → ⊥ write collision.
rule: track ⊥ edit file outside owned paths. shared contract frozen @ wave 0.
cross-track need → raise, ⊥ patch other track path.
**⊥ transient probe files ∈ `src/`. an audit that writes `zz-probe.ts` & self-cleans still breaks `pnpm typecheck` for EVERY other session ∈ the window it exists. probe ∈ the scratchpad — it audits identically & is invisible to the shared tree.

**THE INDEX IS SHARED. `git add <path> && git commit` is ⊥ SAFE.**
`git add` ADDS to an index other sessions are also staging into; `git commit` then commits
the WHOLE index. staging explicitly protects nothing — the sweep happens on the COMMITTER's
side & takes whatever anyone else left staged.
**`git rm` STAGES.** a staged deletion sits ∈ the shared index & rides the next bare commit
from ANY session. for deletions: plain `rm`, then name the path ∈ `git commit -- <paths>`.
that is the door the path rule ⊥ cover.

**`git diff HEAD` before committing catches a STALE EDITOR BUFFER too.** an Edit wrote back a
buffer that predated another session's committed line & silently reverted it; the diff caught it
& the line was restored. the tool-level hazard is the same shape as the index one: what you are
committing is ⊥ only what you typed.

**READ THE INDEX BEFORE COMMITTING: `git diff --cached --stat`.** ⊥ after — printing it ∈ the
same command as the commit shows you the contamination ∈ the output of the thing that already
happened. that is how HEAD got a dangling export: another track's STAGED DELETIONS rode a commit
whose author had named 4 explicit paths of their own.

**PATH SCOPING IS FILE-LEVEL.** `commit -- <paths>` protects against the INDEX; it ⊥ split
co-resident HUNKS inside a file 2 tracks are both editing. the 4th "sweep" was ⊥ a rule breach
— the committer used the correct form & the file was legitimately theirs to commit while ALSO
carrying another track's uncommitted hunks. I diagnosed it as a breach & was wrong.
∴ before committing a SHARED file: `git diff HEAD -- <file>`, eyeball for foreign hunks, &
either coordinate the land order | accept & NOTE the rider ∈ the message.
NUANCE: `-- <paths>` ⊥ reference UNTRACKED files (`pathspec did not match`). for NEW files:
`git add <the new files ONLY>` then `git commit -- <all paths>` — the scoping still holds.
! `git commit -- <paths>` (| `git commit <paths>`): commits ONLY those paths, whatever else
sits ∈ the index.
3 incidents ∈ 1 session. the 3rd was MINE, & my own rule was the insufficient one: I wrote
"explicit paths ∈ `git add`" & then swept 968 lines of a track's staged work into a SPEC
commit while following it. a rule that names the wrong command trains people to feel safe.
⊥ `git add -A` | `git add .` | `git commit -a` while tracks live.** explicit paths ONLY. a track swept 7 files of another session's uncommitted work into its commit; repaired w/ `git restore --staged` (index only, ⊥ worktree) & disclosed. `-A` is ⊥ a convenience here, it is a cross-session data hazard — the sweeping track cannot know what it took. HAPPENED TWICE: the 2nd time a `commit -a` swept another track's STAGED diff into an unrelated spec commit. stage explicit paths, ∀ time.

**GATES THAT LIE — ! know which command actually checks:**
- bare `tsc --noEmit` @ root checks NOTHING & exits 0 (references-only tsconfig, `files: []`). ! `pnpm typecheck`.
- `vitest` ⊥ typecheck. a suite is green while the types are red.
- a unit test on shader SOURCE (`toContain("frameU.time")`) is ⊥ evidence a pixel moved (V147, B15).
∀ 3 have already produced a false green this project. a gate you ⊥ verified is a gate you ⊥ have.

⊥ `git stash` | `git checkout` | any tree-wide git op while tracks live — stash cycles OTHER tracks' uncommitted work. blame a file w/ `git diff HEAD -- <path>`, ⊥ tree-wide state changes.

B263|2026-10-06|**FIXED `4d8687b0` (a workaround and a warning; the bug is Apple's): AN UNSIGNED `/` OR `%` OF A VALUE THAT CAME OUT OF A WRAPPING MULTIPLY AND A SHIFT RETURNS GARBAGE IN A MATERIAL · WGSL (found by shaderloom-f1, Dawn on Metal, M3 Max; `ac5040c9`).** repro, inside a Material · WGSL `surface()` with `pair` a whole-valued f32 from a point attribute: `let a = u32(pair + 0.5); let m = ((a + 2931u) * 2654435761u) >> 16u;`, written to emissive and the byte read back. for pair 5 (m = 35899 on the CPU): `m & 255u` = 59 correct; shifts correct; `(m * 100u) >> 16u` = 54 correct; BUT `m / 97u` came back 386 (true 370), `m % 97u` and `m % 100u` came back at or over 255 (true 9 and 99), and `m - (m / 100u) * 100u` the same; pairs 13–16 each give a different wrong quotient (not one wrong divisor). `(a + 2931u) % 100u`, with no multiply before it, is correct. so multiply, shift and mask agree with the CPU to the bit and only divide and modulo after them do not. NOT TRACED: whether it is Tint's output (its divide and modulo helpers) or Apple's compiler; whether a compute kernel shows it as well as a fragment program. WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE CONSUMER: an integer hash followed by `% n` is the obvious way to draw a lot per instance or per cell, and here it silently disagrees with the same line on the CPU — the stock WGSL (hash and random modules, `// @use` snippets, kernels, the Group predicate) must be searched for the same pattern. wanted: a minimal repro on Dawn in a fragment AND a compute program with exact expected values; the cause named from the generated MSL and Apple's compiler output (as §B260 was read); every stock use found; then a fix at the source (a safe helper the generators emit, or a refusal), and a gate. the consumer scales by multiply and shift instead (`fixtureLot`), held by its `fixtures.gpu.test.ts`. **REPRODUCED THROUGH THE REAL STACK IN BOTH STAGES AND THE CAUSE NAMED (2026-10-06; M3 Max, macOS 26.3.1, one machine, one driver).** a Point Kernel (compute), sixteen points: `m` matches the CPU on all sixteen and `m / 97u`, `m % 97u`, `m % 100u` are wrong on all 48 (m = 35899: 386 for 370, 63993 for 9, 59035 for 99); a Material · WGSL (fragment): the same wrong values. THE CAUSE IS IN APPLE'S DRIVER BACKEND, not Tint and not Apple's front end: Tint's Metal source is right and unsigned; Apple's front end (`xcrun metal -S -emit-llvm`) legally narrows the divide to 16 bits because the value fits (`lshr i32 …, 16` → `trunc … to i16` → `udiv i16 …, 97`), and that IR is still correct; the device returns garbage for exactly that shape. THE SHAPE, pinned by 45 lines on the raw device (512 inputs each): the WHOLE HIGH HALF of a 32-bit value used directly as the dividend of `/` or `%` by a CONSTANT that is not a power of two — `(x >> 16u) / C` and `% C` for C = 3, 10, 97, 100, 255, 1000, `(x / 65536u) % 97u`, `((x >> 8u) >> 8u) % 97u`, the signed and vector forms. the multiply is not needed. RIGHT: a power-of-two divisor, a divisor the shader cannot know, the whole word, a shift by 15, 17, 20, 24 or 25, the low half, a byte or 12 bits of the high half, ANYTHING between the shift and the divide (`((x >> 16u) + 1u) % 97u`), `extractBits(x, 16u, 16u) % 97u`, float, multiply and shift. (the machine code is not visible: "the backend takes the wrong half-register in its divide-by-constant sequence" is a hypothesis; with the high half zero, `/ 3` returns the LOW half over 3.) NO STOCK OR SHIPPED WGSL HAS THE SHAPE: all 9 shifts by 16 in `src/` and all 74 in shipped documents are the xor fold `x ^ (x >> 16u)`, a whole word; the 85 unsigned divides or modulos by a literal in stock sources have vertex indices, faces, cells, ids and float conversions as dividends. not tested: a vertex stage, a browser, another Apple GPU; not searched: author WGSL outside the repository. LEAD'S RULING ON THE FIX (to build after §T1623b slice 2): (a) a stock helper in the hash module for what people want — a lot in 0..n−1 from a hash, `((h >> 16u) * n) >> 16u`, exact against the CPU and a multiply cheaper than a divide — named in the Point Kernel's and Material · WGSL's descriptions; (b) a named WARNING through the Problems registry when an author's WGSL divides a bare high half by a constant (text-level, same function; it says what to write instead; a warning and not a refusal because the WGSL is valid and right on other GPUs; no rewriting of author text — there is no parser to do it safely); (c) a text gate that the shape is absent from both generators' output and every shipped document, a Dawn test that the helper equals the CPU on 512 inputs, and the driver canary kept as a committed tool script to run on an OS or browser bump, not as a gate; (d) the evidence written to `docs/` with a 12-line shader, ready for the OWNER to file with Dawn and Apple (nothing filed). **FIXED AS RULED `4d8687b0` (verified on main: typecheck; both `wgsl-high-half` test files with the generated-text gates and `light-points` 119; on Dawn `hash-lot` and `light-points` 21; the 26 catalogue walkers 444; the gates 59 files / 3,586).** THE BUG IS APPLE'S, NOW PROVEN RATHER THAN INFERRED: a Metal kernel with no Dawn and no Tint returns the same wrong value (`(x >> 16u) % 97u` gives 15872 for x = 96, where the answer is 0), and the Metal source Dawn dumped, run by Metal alone, returns Dawn's wrong values. THE QUOTIENT IS WRONG ONLY THROUGH TINT'S ZERO-DIVISOR GUARD: plain Metal `(x >> 16u) / 97u` is right (Apple's front end folds it into `udiv i32 %x, 6356992`, no 16-bit divide exists); as `a / select(b, 1u, b == 0u)` it is not folded, a `udiv i16` is emitted and the device returns 512 for x = 96; the remainder is wrong in both forms. the trigger read from Apple's compiler output: a `udiv i16` or `urem i16` by a constant that is not a power of two whose dividend is `trunc(lshr i32 x, 16)`; the mechanism inside the driver stays a hypothesis. BUILT: (a) a shared module `lot` (`// @use lot`) with `hashLot(h, n) = ((h >> 16u) * n) >> 16u` and its CPU twin `hashLotReference` (`shared-modules.ts`) — its own module, not part of `hash`, because `WGSL_HASH` is embedded in every Noise shader and adding to it would move every shipped text that includes it; named in the Point Kernel's and Material · WGSL's descriptions. (b) the warning `compiler/wgsl-high-half-divide` (`src/compiler/wgsl-high-half.ts`), delivered at ONE site in the compiler after the plan is read: it reads every pass's text and maps a hit through the pass's source map to the author's node, parameter and line (a kernel, a Material · WGSL named once on the material, a Custom WGSL, a Group predicate; a Geometry's Group has no source map, so its warning lands on the Render with the expression quoted). (c) `wgsl-high-half.cases.ts` is the MEASURED table, 43 lines, 14 wrong and 29 right, and the detector's verdict must equal the device's on every line both ways; `src/examples/wgsl-high-half.test.ts` on `test:gates` holds the shape absent from every pass of every shipped example, every string of all 112 shipped documents, the shared modules and the two lit generators (red with the shape planted in the stock hash module: 45 example passes); `hash-lot.gpu.test.ts` holds `hashLot` equal to its twin for 512 hashes in a kernel and in a Custom WGSL. NOT GATES, tools to run on an OS, driver or browser bump: `tools/apple-gpu-divide-canary.mjs` (today 14 of 14 wrong lines wrong, every right line right) and `tools/apple-gpu-divide-metal.swift`, the pure-Metal reproduction (today 4 of 8 kernels wrong). (d) `docs/apple-gpu-divide-high-half-2026-10-06.md`: the evidence and TWO READY-TO-FILE TEXTS, one for Apple (a Metal kernel) and one for Dawn (a WGSL shader; Tint's guard is what exposes the quotient), each with expected and observed values — NOTHING FILED: the owner's to send. IN INVESTIGATION**: a minimal engine scene first (a floor and N Light nodes), the factors one at a time, the generated WGSL at 4 and 32 lights, compile time by call, then the cause PROVED by a change that removes the growth; a structural cure stops for the lead's ruling because §T1589b slice 1 is in the same generators. **CAUSE FOUND AND PROVEN ON A MINIMAL ENGINE SCENE (interim report, 2026-10-06; one 16×16 floor grid, PBR, N point lights with no shadow, 1280×720, no MSAA, Dawn on Metal, M3 Max, medians of 30 frames with a fixed reference compute pass timed beside every frame).** THE LIT SUM OVER LIGHTS IS ONE STRAIGHT CHAIN OF `lit +=` ACROSS N UNROLLED BLOCKS, and Apple's Metal compiler restructures it (read from `xcrun metal -S -emit-llvm` on the MSL Dawn generates for our text): fast math is on (`reassoc` on every op), so it pulls all 2N per-light terms out of their blocks and sums them in two chains at the END of the fragment function, then SINKS every light's GGX lobe below every light's kind and range branches — the program becomes all branches for all lights, then all lobes, then the sums, and each light's toLight, attenuation and colour stay live across everything. past the register file the fragment program falls off a cliff (that last step is a hypothesis: the machine code is not visible). UNROLLED AS TODAY: 0.05 / 0.13 / 0.33 / 0.39 / 1.51 / 2.88 / 8.52 / 18.7 ms at N = 1 / 8 / 16 / 20 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64 — linear at 0.018 ms a light to 20, ×3.8 between 20 and 24, then faster than N. PROOF: the same blocks, each block's work under `if (lightMeta.y != 0.0) { … }`: 64 lights 18.7 → 1.31 ms, 24 lights 1.50 → 0.46; a loop over an array of rows in the same uniform block: 64 lights 1.11 ms and cold pipeline creation 119 ms against 572. per fragment (64 lights: 2.1 / 5.2 / 19.1 ms at 320 / 640 / 1280 wide). RULED OUT, each by one change at 64 lights: the uniform block's size (the same floats read with trivial code: 0.19 ms), the branches on kind and range (straight-line blocks: 14.0), inlining (a function call per block: 10.6), named members against an array; MSAA, overdraw, mesh and draw count are not needed. A MEASUREMENT TRAP FOUND WITH IT: THE GPU CLOCK FOLLOWS RECENT LOAD — the same 16-light draw took 1.245 ms on an idle GPU and 0.328 ms right after a heavy run, and under contention raw samples go bimodal (19 and 44 ms for one draw); raw milliseconds without a reference pass beside them are not comparable between variants, which bends figures in `docs/lights-from-pointset-design-2026-10-06.md` and may be §B251. COMPILE TIME, first look: Metal caches compiled shaders on disk between processes — a text seen before is 30 ms, a new one 60 ms plus about 8.5 ms a light per distinct lit shader; the 157 → 803 ms above is very likely warm against cold. LEAD'S RULING: (1) a STOPGAP now — each light block's work under the light-is-on test, emitted only when a Render lists more lights than a threshold (8 unless a shipped Render has more), so every shipped text and picture holds byte for byte; gated on the cause (no run of unguarded blocks above the threshold), not on a clock. (2) THE CURE IS STRUCTURAL and pulled forward: named non-casting Lights become rows walked by a loop with a run-time count (§T1623b, now required, the slice after §T1589b slice 1), casting Lights stay blocks each under its own guard at every count; that moves every multi-light Render's text ONCE. (3) every later profile carries a reference pass and alternates variants in one process. still owed by the investigation: the before/after pair on the consumer's document at 37 lights, the §B251 test, the compile-time breakdown, `docs/light-cost-investigation-2026-10-06.md`. **STOPGAP LANDED `97b7d630` (verified on main beside the sheeted grid: typecheck; `scene-light-guard.test`, `generated-text`, `grid-sheets`, `point-sweep` 70; on Dawn `scene-light-guard`, `scene-render`, `point-sweep-sheets` 32; the worker ran the gates 3542).** `LIGHT_GUARD_ABOVE = 8` and `lightGuardWgsl(lightCount)` in `scene-render.wgsl.ts`: above 8 lights each light's block works under a test that the light is on, in BOTH generators (`buildSceneSurfaceModule`, `buildSceneInstancesWgsl`); at and below 8 the text is byte for byte what it was (18 digests taken from main's generator bytes). THE THRESHOLD IS 8 because the cliff sits lower in heavier shaders — stock PBR with no shadow: fine at 20, over at 24; Material · WGSL: fine at 16, over at 20; one casting point light among them: fine at 16, over at 20; both: fine at 12, a timer step apart at 16 — and the guard costs nothing resolvable at 8, 12 or 16; unmeasured: a file mesh with surface rows, several casting lights, a projector or environment in the same shader. PROJECTORS add into the same `lit` (found by the audit) but do NOT lengthen the chain: their addition already sits under two branches on the fragment's own position, so `lit` is a merge after each (8 lights + 0 / 8 / 16 / 24 projectors: 0.131 / 0.262 / 0.328 / 0.459 ms, flat 0.014 ms a projector); the gate counts a projector as a source so one written without its tests fails. THE GATE IS ON THE CAUSE: no more than 8 sources in one straight-line scope of any lit fragment function, 18 cases × with and without casting lights × 1, 8, 9, 32, 64 lights, from both generators (red with the guard off: 108 modules); and on Dawn a 32-light picture equals ambient plus every light's term computed on the CPU at 16 pixels. ON THE CONSUMER'S DOCUMENT (37 lights, live tier, 4× MSAA, alternated in one process, a reference pass beside every frame): 18.35 ms GPU a render → 8.45–8.72; wall 28 → 18 ms; flat 0.075 ms a light with the guard; the cliff today starts near 21 lights there. SHIPPED RENDERS TOUCHED: four on-nothing documents list more than 8 lights (title 13; incar, mcu2, sneaker 9); title's frame at t = 0 through the project's own render differs in 1 of 696,320 pixels by 1 of 255; nothing freezes those documents' text or pictures; every example (7 lights at most) is byte-identical. the stopgap goes when named Lights are rows walked by the loop (§T1623b). still owed: the compile-time breakdown and `docs/light-cost-investigation-2026-10-06.md` with the one-light-path design. **THE INVESTIGATION IS WRITTEN: `docs/light-cost-investigation-2026-10-06.md`, landed `a09acc7a` (sections 0–10 and 12; section 11, the one-light-path design, follows).** THE CAUSE QUANTIFIED from Apple's own output: float components live at once are exactly 39 + 12 a light with main's text (87 at 4 lights, 231 at 16, 807 at 64), 47 at EVERY count with the stopgap, 43 for a loop; that the cliff is register exhaustion stays a hypothesis (the estimate crosses 128 near 8 lights, the cliff is at 20–24). ONE FACTOR AT A TIME at 32 lights, main's text over the stopgap's (ratios only, the run was disturbed): floor 3.7×, 4× MSAA 3.9×, three floors under MSAA 4.7×, a 293,000-triangle floor 4.5×, primitive boxes 3.9×, Phong 2.0×, directional 5.0×, no Range 4.1×. COMPILE TIME SETTLED: cold three times over with a salted text against warm — the minimal floor's three render pipelines, main / stopgap / loop: 86 / 88 / 36 ms at 16 lights, 189 / 149 / 36 at 32, 462 / 278 / 36 at 64, warm 2–14; the consumer's document, `backend.compile` cold with main's text: 508 ms at 5 lights, 559 at 13, 734 at 21, 1,022 at 37, warm 174–243 at every count. so the "157 → 803 ms between 5 and 13 lights" at the top of this row was WARM AGAINST COLD plus about 300 ms the first cold compile of a process pays; like for like it is 51 ms. 36 modules, 27 render and 9 compute pipelines at every light count; five distinct lit texts for 16 draws, none compiled twice (one non-lit text, `geometry_hull:instances:resolve`, is created twice: a module creation, no Metal compile). TWO MORE MEASUREMENT TRAPS: a lone render pass that clears and draws straight after a compute pass reads 0.07 or 0.85 ms for the same draw (encoded as the backend does, a clearing pass then a loading pass, it is steady); a cache-busting salt must survive Tint's constant folding and f32 rounding. a claim WITHDRAWN in the writing: "a pass of its own costs the lit draw 0.4 ms" was a pair from before the reference existed. THE CASTING-LIGHTS PROTOTYPE (for section 11): one loop with every shadow a layer of ONE texture array costs the same as today's blocks within a timer step at 1, 2, 4 and 8 casting point lights, with one texture binding instead of N and a text that does not grow; per-light softness as loop bounds costs 1.7×, as a choice between constant loops nothing. the reference harness is `makeReference` in the session scratch (`scratchpad/b260/minimal.ts`, 30 lines; its WGSL and protocol are section 2 of the document) — to become a tool of the test harness (§T1635b).|T1589b,T1623b

V1011|⚡⚡⚡**GENERATED TEXT IS ⊥ PER-FRAME WORK. IF AN OUTPUT IS DETERMINED ENTIRELY BY INPUTS THAT DO ⊥ CHANGE BETWEEN FRAMES, RECOMPUTING IT EVERY FRAME IS A DEFECT — ⊥ A COST TO BUDGET.** measured (§T1330b): `codegen.ts` is **39.4 % OF ALL SCRIPT @ IDLE** on the heaviest shipped document, regenerating WGSL text inside `compile()`, which runs every frame. **EVERY INPUT TO IT IS STRUCTURAL; ⊥ ONE DEPENDS ON TIME.** ⚑**THE CAUSE IS A CONFLATION WORTH NAMING BECAUSE IT RECURS: THE FRAME PATH ASKS "DID THIS NODE *CHANGE*?" & ACTS ON THE ANSWER, BUT A NODE WHOSE *VALUES* CHANGED HAS ⊥ NECESSARILY CHANGED ITS *SOURCE*. ONE QUESTION, TWO ANSWERS, & THE EXPENSIVE ONE WAS ASSUMED.** ∴ **SEPARATE THE TWO EXPLICITLY @ EVERY BOUNDARY WHERE WORK IS SKIPPED: WHAT DEPENDS ON *TIME* (uniforms, values) & WHAT DEPENDS ON *STRUCTURE* (source, passes, layouts). CACHE THE SECOND ON A KEY *DERIVED* FROM ITS INPUTS, NEVER HAND-LISTED** (§V982). ⛑**THE ASSERTION THAT PROVES IT IS *REFERENCE IDENTITY ACROSS A TIME-ONLY STEP*, ⊥ VALUE EQUALITY: `===` ON THE EMITTED STRING. VALUE EQUALITY PASSES WHILE THE WORK IS STILL BEING DONE ∴ IT CANNOT DISTINGUISH "CACHED" FROM "REGENERATED IDENTICALLY", WHICH IS THE ENTIRE QUESTION.** ⛑**& THE CACHE'S OWN KNOWN POSITIVE IS ITS *INVALIDATION*: a cache that never invalidates passes an identity test PERFECTLY & ships a stale shader — worse than the slowness it cured. RED-VERIFY BY CHANGING A CODEGEN-AFFECTING INPUT & WATCHING THE TEXT CHANGE** (§V968). ⛑**OWNER'S FRAMING, & IT IS THE STANDARD: *"never do this per frame without a reason, without a change to it — this is supposed to be a LIVE TOOL."* A LIVE TOOL'S FRAME BUDGET IS SPENT ON WHAT CHANGED.** ⛑⛑⚠**THE GATE THIS ROW SPECIFIED IS *WRONG* & IS RETRACTED HERE (§T1335b). "ASSERT THE EMITTED SOURCE IS THE SAME OBJECT BY `===`" CANNOT WORK ON A *STRING*: A STRING IS A PRIMITIVE, SO `===` & `Object.is` COMPARE BY *VALUE*** — orchestrator verified: two independently built `'abc'+'def'` are `===` true. **∴ THE IDENTITY ASSERTION IS GREEN UNDER A CACHE THAT NEVER CACHES, WHICH IS THE EXACT FAILURE THIS ROW WAS WRITTEN TO PREVENT.** d0 found it by WRITING the test & having two of its assertions fail (§V976 — the instrument finds the bug): *"the test was wrong, ⊥ the code."* **∴ A STRING-KEYED MEMO'S *HIT* IS UNOBSERVABLE FROM OUTSIDE IT, & THE ONLY HONEST INSTRUMENTS ARE CORRECTNESS-UNDER-CHANGE & THE PROFILE** (→§V1013). **THE REST OF THIS ROW STANDS: generated text is ⊥ per-frame work, the values/source conflation is real, & the cache's known positive is its INVALIDATION. V1029|**GENERATED TEXT IS A FUNCTION OF WHAT A NODE IS, NEVER OF HOW MANY THE DOCUMENT HAS.** a count the author raises by adding items (lights, projectors, casters, inputs, layers, strips, attributes) is DATA: rows in a buffer or layers of a texture array walked by a loop with a run-time count, a count in a uniform, or a loop region with its count in the plan; compiled at N and at 2N, every shader text is byte-identical. EXCEPTIONS, each a ledger row with its bound and its reason: (a) a count the definition fixes; (b) one DECLARATION per item where the language forces it (a binding per texture, a member and an accessor per schema attribute), as declarations and independent statements only, under a named refusal at a stated count (a byte bound that implies a count is a stated count); (c) one PASS per item reusing a shared text; (d) a chain that carries one value across items ONLY under a named refusal at a bound of 8 or fewer items, with a measurement on record (a reference pass beside every frame) that its cost is linear up to the bound — Composite's fold is the one known case. NEVER: a function body that grows per item while carrying a value across items, unbounded — that is §B260 (N unrolled light blocks in one `lit` chain: past about 20 the Metal compiler keeps every block's values live at once and the frame goes from 0.4 to 18.7 ms at 64). held by `src/compiler/generated-text-growth.test.ts` on `test:gates` (§T1635b): every count axis derived from the registry is compiled at 1, 2, 4, 16 and held to one law (flat, literal, declarations, statements), a chain being allowed only in a `NOT_YET_DATA` list with a task id and an exactly asserted length that can only go down. owner, 2026-10-06: *"we do the real cure right so it becomes a core fix of the whole app and not an inplace shader trick of a single patch"*. AS THE GATE HOLDS IT (`f5fa2e85`): two more laws are named and are not growth — LITERAL (a compile-time number written into the text: a new text a value, the same size, bounded by the parameter's maximum; 11 axes) and BRANCH (one text for one, another for several, identical beyond: `pointTopology.sheets`).
